answer: Replica keys fail a kiln that fires only one plaque. A key stakes 1.86 POA and claims a single jade plaque on a public ocean quay, etched with a 23-byte hash. Over 18 hours it must lay five saffron washes, each a 15-byte coat signed from a fresh /22 and bound to the live tip and that hash. Three judges recompute each coat and reject a reused ASN or two washes under 80 minutes. If four plaques open under one wallet in 9 hours, or two plaques share three coat prefixes, all shatter and the 1.86 POA stays sunk. A missed wash leaves the plaque unfired; no second berth is issued.
